resources.string: Maintenance opens capabilities you name, for a bounded time, and then puts the previous policy back. Nothing is opened by default, and nothing is reported as open until this device has confirmed it.
Open selected capabilities for a bounded service visit
Checking whether a maintenance window is open…
The system policy controls configured on this device are the whole policy right now.
Choose only what the task needs. Each capability relaxes the controls named under it and nothing else, and a capability the base policy was not enforcing changes nothing.
Opens a privileged transport rather than a feature. It is never selected for you, it is never implied by another capability, and it needs its own confirmation.
The closing time is an estimate read from the clock of this device. The window itself is timed from the boot clock, so moving the date or time cannot extend it, and a restart closes it.
This is what leaves protection, and for how long.

The window closes when it expires, when the device restarts, and when you close it by hand. In every one of those cases the previous policy is applied again and read back before the window is reported as closed.
This confirmation is separate because this decision is separate.
With developer options and USB debugging open, a cable and an authorised host can drive this device outside everything this console enforces, including the application allowlist and the kiosk.
Do not leave it open. Close the window as soon as the task is finished rather than waiting for it to expire, and check afterwards that the status card reads closed.
The window has run out. It is being closed and the previous policy restored.
No control had to be turned off, because the base policy was not enforcing any of them.
The maintenance window was applied and read back on this device.
This device did not confirm the window, so it was undone. The previous policy was applied again and read back. Device response: %1$s
This device confirmed neither the window nor the restore that followed it, so some restrictions may still be relaxed. Device response: %1$s
The window is closed and the previous policy was read back in force on this device.
The window is over, but this device did not confirm the previous policy. Device response: %1$s
The previous policy was not confirmed

Treat this device as relaxed until it reports otherwise. Close the window again from here; if it keeps failing, apply and verify the system policy controls from the policy console, then restart the device before it goes back into service.
The administrator session expired, so no maintenance window can be requested.
System administration is not configured on this device, so no restriction can be relaxed.
A window is already open. Close it first: widening a window means closing the current one, verifying the restore, and opening a new one that is recorded on its own.
Select at least one capability. Maintenance opens nothing by default.
Choose one of the offered durations.
A maintenance window is already open.
The request named a capability this build does not know.
The requested length is not a positive duration.
The requested length is longer than this build grants.
Every installer on the device can run again for the length of the window, including an application store. Device Guard can also install its own signed updates while this is open.

A package file already on the device can be installed. If the base policy also blocks all package installation, that control keeps blocking this until you open the stores and installers capability as well; the window says so rather than opening it for you.
Force stop, clear data and clear cache become available in Settings. Date and time, users and profiles, factory reset and Safe Boot are not part of this capability and stay closed.
The device can be mounted as storage over a cable, so files can be copied on and off it during the visit.

Developer options and ADB become available. A cable and an authorised host can then drive this device outside everything this console enforces. This is a privileged transport rather than a feature: open it only for the task that needs it, and close the window as soon as that task is finished.
The maintenance window reached its end time.
The maintenance window ended because the device restarted.
An administrator closed the maintenance window.
The maintenance window was closed because the clock readings could not be trusted.
A stored maintenance record could not be read, so the previous policy was restored.
The maintenance window was undone because opening it could not be verified.
Maintenance window refused or not verified: %1$s
Maintenance window closed and policy restored: %1$s
